Find the smallest design that meets a target

Source: R/smallest-design.R
smallest_design.Rd

Reads a grid summary design by design and returns, for each group of rows, the smallest value of along (by default the number of trials) at which a target is met and stays met at every larger value in the grid. A design meets a target when the lower end of the target's Monte Carlo interval clears it, so the answer accounts for how many replications the grid ran.

Usage

smallest_design(
  x,
  target,
  along = "n_trials",
  by = "n_subjects",
  level = 0.95,
  coverage_check = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A grid summary that carries the design columns (summary() of a recovery_grid() result), or such a recovery object, which is summarised first. Filter it first to the rows the question is about, for example level == "subject".

target

A named numeric vector of thresholds on summary columns, such as c(r_low = 0.8) or c(reliability_model = 0.8, precision_met = 0.8). Higher is better for every column allowed: detected, sign_recovery, precision_met, reliability_true, reliability_model, r_low and ccc_low.

along

The design column to minimise.

by

Design columns that define separate groups, each with its own answer; NULL for none. Every grid column that varies besides along belongs here: each group must have one row per value of along (and term, level and estimator), or the call is refused.

level

The mass of the Monte Carlo interval whose lower end must clear the target.

coverage_check

If TRUE, a design counts as meeting a target only when every population row at that design also has its coverage within one MCSE of nominal, abs(coverage - ci_level) <= coverage_mcse. This is a calibration condition, not a target. It reads the population rows left in x, so keep them (their groups drop out of the answer when the target column is NA there), and a design with none fails the check.

Value

A bmmtools_smallest_design tibble with one row per by group, term, level, estimator and target: the by columns, term, level, estimator, target (the column), threshold, smallest (the certified value of along, or NA), smallest_point (the same rule applied to the point estimate, which shows what Monte Carlo error costs), status, and replications_needed, the replications a perfect rate would need to certify the threshold when that is why a design is undecided (NA otherwise). Printing it states each answer as a sentence.

Details

The lower end. For a rate (detected, sign_recovery, precision_met) it is the Wilson score bound, because the plain MCSE of a rate is 0 at 0 and 1 and would certify a target from three successes in three. Its count is the effective sample size p (1 - p) / MCSE^2: the number of intervals when the MCSE is binomial, and at the subject level a number corrected for subjects of one fit not being independent, capped at the number of intervals. At a rate of 0 or 1, or an MCSE of 0, the number of replications is used, so a perfect rate certifies 0.80 only from 16 replications on. For a reliability it is estimate - z * MCSE. r_low and ccc_low are already lower ends and are read as they are; level does not change them. r, ccc and ci_width have no Monte Carlo interval and are refused, naming the column to use. coverage is refused too: "high enough" is the wrong question for a coverage, which coverage_check asks properly.

Monotone in the grid. Noise that lets 30 trials pass and 100 fail does not produce 30. A consequence is that several targets, or several terms, are met together from the largest of their single answers, which is how a condition on every parameter is read off.

No interpolation, no extrapolation. status is "met", "met at the grid's smallest design" (the true minimum may be lower), "not reached in this grid", or "undecided: too few replications" (the point estimate meets the target, the bound does not). A group whose target column is NA at every design, such as a reliability on population rows, is left out.

Examples

summary(recovery_mixture2p) |>
  dplyr::filter(level == "subject") |>
  smallest_design(c(r_low = 0.8))
#> <bmmtools_smallest_design>
#> n_subjects = 20, kappa (subject), r_low >= 0.8: not reached in this grid.
#> n_subjects = 20, thetat (subject), r_low >= 0.8: met from n_trials = 100.
#> n_subjects = 50, kappa (subject), r_low >= 0.8: not reached in this grid.
#> n_subjects = 50, thetat (subject), r_low >= 0.8: met from n_trials = 100.
